html:
The Yucatec Maya are the Maya people of the Yucatán peninsula, in today's Mexican states of Yucatán, Campeche and Quintana Roo and in northern Belize. Their language, Maaya t'aan, is spoken by some 800,000 people, one of the largest Indigenous languages in Mexico.

They are heirs of the northern Maya city-states, such as Chichén Itzá. After the fall of Mayapan in the mid 1400s, Yucatán split into about sixteen small provinces, each with its own lord. That was the situation in 1492.

The Spanish needed some twenty years to conquer them. Francisco de Montejo began the war in 1527, and his son of the same name founded Mérida in 1542. Under Spanish rule Maya villages paid tribute and labour, and friars burned their books, though a few codices survived. In 1847 Maya peasants rose in the Caste War of Yucatán, and rebel Maya held the east of the peninsula until 1901. Neighbours: Mopan and Lacandon.
